subject: Reden Health - branch cutover caused inconsistent egress path and failing API responses
messages:
From: Reden Health <infra@redenhealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent 502s after branch cutover - API timeouts

Hi Dylan,

We cut over our new branch router at 08:50 PDT and since then ~15% of our inbound API requests to the /v1/payments endpoint are returning 502 / connection reset. The issue is intermittent and seems to affect larger payload responses (~1.6-2MB). Small responses look fine.

Attached is a traceroute from our gateway to your edge (initial-trace.txt). We also captured a few tcpdumps — I'll upload the full pcaps if you want, but I included a short snippet in the trace file.

Key observations from our side:
- The path sometimes routes to a different Internet egress appliance (10.240.3.11) instead of your expected egress (10.240.1.5) after BGP flap.
- When the alternate egress is used we see the client source IP rewritten to a different SNAT pool and the server closes the TCP connection during TLS/HTTP response.

Can you triage? We rely on Redwood private deployment for low-latency payments and this is customer-impacting.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Infra Lead, Reden Health

--
Attachment: initial-trace.txt (plain text, 2.2 KB)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s after branch cutover - API timeouts

Triage notes (summary):
- I reviewed the initial-trace.txt and a short pcap Sanjay sent over to our secure upload. I pulled edge logs for the customer prefix (203.55.120.0/24) between 08:45-09:15 PDT.

Findings:
1) Asymmetric egress observed: ~30% of flows exit via alternate egress appliance (10.240.3.11) with a different SNAT pool. Return packets arrive back to the customer via the expected appliance (10.240.1.5) — packets are getting routed differently on the on-prem/branch side. This creates TCP state mismatch and results in resets.

2) MTU/fragmentation surface: the failing responses are large (~1.6MB). We see TCP retransmits and ICMP Fragmentation Needed (DF set) in the pcap when routed via the alternate path. The alternate egress path goes through a firewall that clamps MSS inconsistently. That combination causes large TLS records to be dropped mid-response.

3) Security group / ephemeral port behavior: The branch firewall is applying a policy that limits high ephemeral port ranges (client-side) for return traffic on the alternate appliance. When SNAT uses the different pool, the firewall treats the session as external and times out ephemeral mappings earlier than the primary path — this results in late-stage connection resets.

Suggested immediate mitigations (short-lived, low-risk):
- Add a static route on the branch router for Redwood edge ranges (10.240.0.0/16) pointing at the primary egress (10.240.1.5) for a canary subset (start with 203.55.120.0/25) so affected customers are forced back to the known-good path.
- Configure a temporary MSS clamp on the alternate firewall to 1350 to avoid fragmentation (apply to egress peer IP 10.240.3.11).
- Add a temporary SNAT bypass for 203.55.120.0/24 on the alternate appliance (policy-based NAT exception) so source IPs are preserved.
- Expand ephemeral port allowance 32768-61000 on the branch firewall for return packets to Redwood egress pools.

Longer-term recommendations:
- Update BGP/local path selection so the branch prefers primary egress for Redwood prefixes, or implement route dampening on the alternate appliance to avoid flipping for short-lived flaps.
- Add monitoring synthetic tests that exercise large payload responses to catch MTU-related regressions.

Attachments: I uploaded a trimmed pcap (tcpdump-12.pcap) showing the ICMP Fragmentation Needed and a sample conntrack line. See attached.

I can prepare the exact cli commands/config snippets for the branch vendor (Juniper/Arista) and the firewall (Palo Alto) if you want.

--
Attachment: tcpdump-12.pcap (pcap, 1.1 MB)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s after branch cutover - API timeouts

Thanks Marissa — good triage. I'm proposing the following rollout for mitigation (need approval to execute):

Plan (canary -> roll):
1) 15:00-15:30 PDT: Apply static route for 203.55.120.0/25 -> 10.240.1.5 on branch router (canary block). Monitor edge logs and customer feedback for 30 minutes. Rollback if any unexpected traffic blackholing occurs.
2) 15:30-15:40 PDT: Apply MSS clamp 1350 on alternate firewall egress to avoid fragmentation.
3) 15:40-16:00 PDT: Add policy NAT bypass for 203.55.120.0/24 on alternate appliance and expand ephemeral port range.
4) 16:00-16:30 PDT: If canary stable, expand static route to whole customer prefix; then schedule a follow-up config change to BGP/local-preference to make primary egress preferred.

Risk and rollback:
- Static route misconfig can blackhole traffic — we'll pre-stage the configuration and test with a single /25.
- SNAT bypass has minimal risk (only affects traffic to Redwood prefixes) but policy order matters; we'll stage at a low precedence.

I need sign-off from Dylan to schedule the window and from Vanessa for change coordination with the branch ops team. I'll prepare the exact CLI snippets and a change ticket (RJ-5821). Runbook for private egress triage: https://runbook.redwood.ai/private-egress-triage

Karthik
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
